title: Ovarian Cancer Detection Using Photoacoustic Flow Cytometry
protocol: Filter approximately 300 mL of deionized water through a 0.2 μm sterile filter.
Clean a 250 mL glass round bottom flask with a detergent solution and rinse with DI water.
Add 0.0134 g of CuCl2 into 100 mL of DI water to create a 1 mM solution.
Add 0.015 g of folic acid (FA) to the CuCl2 solution and stir for ~5 min using a magnetic stir bar.
Add Na2S·9H2O (0.024 g in 100 μL DI water) over approximately 10 s to the reaction mixture utilizing a 200 μL pipette.
Cap the reaction and place in an oil bath set to 90 °C, continuing stirring with a magnetic stir bar.
Vent the system while heating the reaction mixture to avoid pressure buildup.
Allow the reaction to proceed for an additional hour after reaching 85−90 °C.
Briefly cool the reaction vessel at room temperature for approximately 10 to 15 min before transferring to an ice bath.
Adjust the pH to 10 utilizing 1M NaOH to dissolve remaining folic acid into solution.
Purify the FA-CuS reaction mixture using a 30 kDa centrifugation column.
Add solution in 15 mL batches to the column and centrifuge at 3,082 x g for 15 min.
Wash 4x with 15 mL of pH 10 NaOH in the 30 kDa centrifugation column.
Take 1/3 of the solution (~66 µL) and split into three glass vials.
Dry in a vacuum oven overnight at 40 °C under a vacuum of ~27 mmHg.
Dissolve the other 2/3 of concentrated solution into 250 µL of PBS.
Store the dissolved solution at 4 °C until further use.
Sonicate FA-CuS NPs for 30 min in a bath sonicator on a high setting prior to utilization.
Perform dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Add 10 µL of concentrated FA-CuS NPS in PBS solution to 2 mL of DI water.
Prior to characterization by DLS, sonicate the particles for 30 min in a bath sonicator on a high setting.
Filter through a 0.2 µm sterile filter to remove residual dust.
Add 10 μL of concentrated FA-CuS NPS in PBS solution to a piece of wax paper.
Invert a formvar coated copper grid on the top of the droplet and let sit for 2 min.
Touch the edge of the formvar-coated grid to a piece of filter paper to remove excess liquid.
Let air dry.
Image the copper grid utilizing an electron microscope at an accelerating voltage of 80 kV.
Add Texas-Red-X succinimidyl ester to a solution containing FA-CuS NPs in 1 mL of 0.1 M NaHCO3 buffer and stir for 1 hour away from light.
Concentrate the reaction mixture in a 4 mL 30 kDa MWCO centrifugation column by spinning at 4,000 x g for 10 min.
Wash the concentrated solution with 4 mL of 0.1 M NaHCO3 buffer three times.
Subsequently wash the concentrated solution with 4 mL of DI water three times or until only a trace amount of fluorescence remains visible in the flowthrough by UV-VIS.
Incubate SKOV-3 cells in a T75 flask with 8−15 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 media containing 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin for at least 24 h.
Seed cells in 0.5 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 complete growth media at a density of 0.1 x 10^6 cells/mL into a 24 well plate.
Incubate cells with 400 µg/mL FA-CuS NPS in 0.5 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 complete growth media for 2 h.
Trypsinize the cells with 0.5 mL of 0.25% trypsin with EDTA.
Add at least 1 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 complete growth media to neutralize the trypsin.
Centrifuge the cells at 123 x g for 6 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 2 mL of PBS and centrifuge at 123 x g for 6 min.
Repeat the wash step 2x to remove unbound NPs.
Resuspend the cells in 1−2 mL of PBS with 2% Tween solution.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer and trypan blue.
Dilute cells in PBS with 2% Tween to the chosen concentration for detection if cell counts are too high.
Seed cells at a density of 0.1 x 10^6 cells/mL in 0.5 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 complete growth media on glass coverslips in a 24 well plate for microscopy analysis.
Incubate the cells with fluorescently tagged FA-CuS NPs in triplicate.
Use concentrations of 100 µg/mL, 200 µg/mL, 300 µg/mL, and 400 µg/mL in 0.5 mL of folic-acid-free RPMI-1640 complete growth media.
Incubate the cells with NPs for 2 h at 37 °C.
Wash the cells 3 times with PBS carefully without disturbing the cells.
Add PBS solution to the side of the well plate and tilt the plate to withdraw the solution.
Incubate the cells with 0.5 mL of 3.7% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 15 min.
Transfer glass coverslips to a new 24-well plate.
Incubate the cells in a solution of 3.7% PFA and 0.1% Triton-X in PBS for 5 min.
Wash the cells with 0.5 mL of PBS 3 times for 5 min each and transfer coverslips to a new plate.
Incubate the cells with 0.5 mL of a PBS solution containing DAPI (20 µL/mL of a 0.5 mg/mL stock solution) for 5 min, away from light.
Wash the cells with PBS 3 times.
Mount the coverslips on slides with mounting medium.
The cells are now ready to be imaged by fluorescence microscopy.
3D print the flow tank using ABS thermoplastic or PLA plastic.
Clean and assemble the system for use after printing the 3D flow tank.
Place glass coverslips over the 1 mm x 3 mm slot and the 1 cm hole in the flow system.
Seal with silicone to prevent leakage over the slots and holes.
Fit the capillary tube into the silicone cured tubes.
Insert the tubes into the flow chamber through the side of the flow tank such that the glass capillary tube is directly above and in front of the 3 mm slot and the 1 cm hole.
Seal the tubing using silicone to prevent leakage.
Connect the transducer to an ultrasound pulser/receiver.
Amplify the signal with a 59 dB gain.
Connect the output of the filter to a multipurpose reconfigurable oscilloscope equipped with a built-in field programmable gate array.
Fill one syringe pump with air and the other pump with the sample to be analyzed.
Set the pump containing air to a flow rate of 40 µL/min.
Set the pump containing the sample to a flow rate of 20 µL/min.
Connect one tube from the flow chamber to a T-junction, connected to two syringe pumps at each branch.
Fill one of the tubes with air and the other with the sample to be analyzed.
Lightly vortex each sample immediately before being tested.
Rotate the syringe every few minutes to prevent cells from settling in the solution.
Connect the remaining tube exiting the flow system to a container with 10% bleach for disposal of cells after testing.
Place the section of the quartz capillary tube in direct alignment with the transducer.
Ensure the optical fiber illuminates the entire width of the tube when placed above the sample.
Irradiate the sample using an optical fiber channeling a diode-pumped solid state laser operating at 1,053 nm.
Place the flow system on top of an inverted microscope.
Ensure both the laser pulse and the path of the sample are visible as it passes through the system.
Record flow using a microscope-mounted camera.
Record ultrasound acquisitions utilizing data acquisition software.
Trigger ultrasound and pulsed laser using the FPGA.
Utilize PBS with 2% Tween as the negative control.
Use FA-CuS NPs at a concentration of 100 µg/mL in PBS 2% Tween as the positive control.
Record both the firing of the laser and the passage of samples through the flow system using a microscope-mounted camera.
Correlate the acoustic signal recorded by the transducer with the firing of the laser.
Illuminate each plug several times at a sampling rate of 10 Hz as the samples pass in front of the laser.
Calculate the Hilbert transform, H[s(t)], for each signal acquisition s(t).
Create a complex envelope se(t) by calculating the magnitude of the analytic signal.
Integrate the envelope to measure the total signal resulting from each acquisition.
Compare signals from different test groups (i.e., PBS, tagged cells, FA-CuS NPs, cells alone) using a t-test in R statistical software.
Normalize the complex envelope based on the maximum peak across the whole run for image reconstruction.
If comparing a series of runs, normalize the complex envelope using the maximum peak across the entire series.
Convert each acquisition into a series of pixel values after normalization.
Represent each series of pixel values as a column in the image reconstruction.
